variantDescriptions.fixyoung: base with `-Xmn3g -XX:-G1UseAdaptiveIHOP`: young gen fixed at 3G (G1 picks about 2.8G here), so young GCs fall at allocation points rather than where the pause-time feedback puts them
variantDescriptions.xbatch: base with `-Xbatch`: compiles block the requesting thread, so allocation (escape analysis) is nearly deterministic (`m4-noise-scala`: alloc CV 0.04%)
variantDescriptions.xbatchfix: both: deterministic allocation and fixed GC points, so weak references in `uniques` are cleared at the same points in every fork

name: m4-forkvar-gc
description: Is fork-to-fork variance in instructions/op GC-coupled through the type uniques table? `Types.uniques` is a `WeakHashSet`: a young GC clears entries for types no longer reachable, and a later `unique` of an equal type then rebuilds it and its per-instance caches. G1's adaptive young sizing follows measured pause times, so GC points move between forks even with deterministic allocation. 2x2 of `-Xbatch` (deterministic allocation) and a fixed young gen (GC points by allocation). Read each variant's spread of instructions/op; means are not comparable between variants.
